caseno: Appeal from Appellate Decree No. 770 of 1959.
lawyer:
Shehabullah  with Moqbul Ahmed ----- For the appellants.
A.K.M. Shafiqur Rahman with Faruque Ahmed ----- For the respondents.
parties:
Abdul Hamid & ors ----- Appellants
Vs.
Abul Hossain Mir being dead, his heirs: Abdus Sobhan Mir & ors ----- Respondent
full_judgment:
2. Plaintiffs have alleged that the suit properties belonged to Arman Mir and Jamiruddin Mir and that the two brothers who were in ejamali possession of the properties had 8 annas share each therein. On the basis of geneology through Jamiruddin Mir the plaintiff have jointly claimed 4 annas 2 gondas 1 kara 5 krantis share in the properties. The plaintiffs have further alleged that C S. dag Nos. 100 and 10l have been wrongly recorded in the suit khatian No. 146 and that these two plots have been acquired by the sons of Jamiruddia from one Barkat by a kabala dated 24th Ashar 1306 B.S, and these plots have been wrongly recorded in the khatianas properties owned by the co-sharers on the basis of inheritance from Arman Mir and Jamiruddin Mir. 

 3. The defendant Nos. 2, 19, 35 and 45 by two separate written statements contested the suit They have alleged that Arman Mir and Jamiruddin Mir were not full brothers but they were step brothers: they lived in a different village; Arman Mir first came over to this village and settled down and acquired the properties thereafter Jamiruddin Mir came to reside with his step brother Arman Mir and that both of them acquired sepal rate independent properties. Subsequently there had been a partition between the superior landlords under the Estate Partition Act in which the personal properties acquired by Arman Mir were recorded in the Batwara Khatin No. 38 and the other properties belonging to Jamiruddin Mir and Arman Mir in equal shares were recorded in the Batwara Khatian No. 39 it has been contended that during the last C S. operation, the properties of Batwara Khatian Nos. 38 and 39 were fraudulently recorded in the suit khatian. i.e. C.S. Khatian No. 146; properties recorded in Batwara khatian No 38 have been wrongly included in the suit kharian No. 146 of Dhaneswar Mouja; and these are not liable to be partitioned in this suit. 

 In the trial the principal point for determination was whether the lands in Batwara Khatian No. 38 were self-acquired properties of Arman Mir or joint properties of the two brothers and which khatian would prevail over the other. 

 5. Mr. Shehabullah with Mr. Moqbul Ahmed the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant-appellants has submitted that the court of appeal below committed an error of law in affirming the decree of the trial solely on the basis of entries in the C.S. Khatian inasmuch as that when the court has embarked upon an investigation of the title of the respective parties to the suit properties the entry in the khatian lost its weight and more so when the plaintiffs have failed to prove the basis of the eatries in the khatian. He has submitted that the plaintiffs having failed to produce any evidence as regards the basis of the entries in the khatian both the courts below committed an error of law in decreeing the suit on the basis of the entries in C.S. Khatian alone. In support of his contentions he has referred to the decisions reported in 17 DLR (SC)-398, 14 DLR 725 and 27 DLR 589. He has also submitted that the courts below ought to have accepted the entries in the batwara khatians and the rent receipts in support of the contentions of the defendant that the properties in batwara khatian No. 38 were the self-acquired properties of Arman Mir. 

 6. Mr. A.K.M. Sha6qur Rahman, the Jearned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondents has submitted that presumption of khtians loses its weight with the passage of time and that the entries in the subsequent khatian would be more acceptable to a court than the entree in the earlier khatian. According to him the latter Khatian should relatively have more weight than the previous one. He has further submitted that the presumption of the C.S. Khatian which is subsequent in point of time was rightly accepted by the courts below than those in the batwara khatian; according to him the C.S. khatian having been prepared subsequently in 1915-18 should prevail over the batwara khatian prepared in 1908 inasmuch that the earlier Batwara khatian must be deemed to have been considered and rejected. He has also submitted that the court of appeal below accepting the evidence of the witnesses of the P.Ws. has found that the plaintiffs’ predecessor Jamiruddin Mir possessed the suit land i.e. the lands of batwara khatain No. 38. 

 7. As regards the presumption of the C. S. Khatian upon which the courts below have held that the suit properties originally belonged to Arman Mir and Jamiruddin Mir, it appears that apart from the presumption of the C.S. Khatians, the trial court has elaborately considered the oral evidence of the witnesses of the plaintiff. Court of appeal below has considered the evidence of P.W. Wasuddin aged about 90 years. This witness has denied that Amiruddin Mir and Jamiruddin Mir came to this place from a southern country. He has deposed that Arman Mir and Jamiruddin Mir are the sons of Dhanai Mir. Other witnesses of the plaintiff have deposed that the suit lands were possessed by the heirs of Arman Mir and Jamiruddin Mir. The trial court has also considered the oral evidence of the witnesses for the defendants 

 8. Defendants have alleged that properties described in batwara khatian No. 38 appertaining to jote No. II were the self-acquired properties of Arman Mir and that the properties in Batwara khatain No. 39 were the joint properties of Arman Mir and Jamiruddin Mir. The defendants have alleged that properties in batwara khatian No. 39 also belonged to Arman Mir but since these comprise of homestead and sat lands Arman Mir allowed Jamiruddin Mir to stay there and ultimately gave the said land to the latter and as such the names of two brothers Arman and Jamiruddin Mir have been recorded in the Batwara Khatian No. 39. In support of the tenancy of Arman Mir in respect of khatian No. 39 the defendants have produced some rent receipts B series, to prove original tenancy of Arman Mir with respect to the lands of Batwara No. 38. Court of Appeal below in this connection observed that by the dakhilas ext. B series showing payment of rents with respect to the entire lands of the khatians, the interest of the co-sharers remain unaffected. It is also seen from the dakhilas that all the heirs of Arman Mir have not paid rents by these dakhilas. Be that as it may the payment of rent by itself does not prove that heirs of Arman Mir only were the tenants of the land of C.S. Khatian No. 146. 

 9. The batwara khatian has been prepared in 1908 whereas the C.S Khatian has been prepared in 1915-18. The C.S. Khatian having been prepared subsequently in point of time is more acceptable than the earlier khatian. In a decision reported in 38 C.W.N. 268 it has been held that in case of assessment of relative value of two khatians, the latest khatian should prevail over the earlier khatian. On this question their lordships in that decision has held as follows:- 

 10. In my view the presumption that was attached to the batwara khatian lost its relative weight after C S. Khatian came into being in 1915-18. In the absence of any other evidence the latter khatian was rightly accepted by the courts below in proof of the state of affairs existed at the time when the records were prepared and that the presumption of the C.S, Khatian in my view could not be rebutted by the defendants by any cogent evidences and the courts below correctly accepted the entries in the C.S. records. I am further of the opinion that the presumption of the C.S. Khatian did not lose its weight because of absence of evidence as to its basis (14 D.L.R. 725). It further appears that the trial court has also noticed the evidence of D.Ws. 7 and 8 who are heirs of Arman Mir. They have claimed their saham on the basis that the properties belonged to Arman Mir and Jamiruddin Mir. If they have supported the case of the defendants they could claim a double share than what they have claimed by an application for saham.
